references.text: Continuation of the same law text concerning uncleanness and peace offerings, elaborating on what kind of impurity leads to being cut off from the people.
Concerns that anyone who is unclean and approaches the holy gifts shall be cut off from the Lord's presence - the same principle regarding impurity and holy things.
Also mentions the punishment of being cut off from the people for profaning what is holy to the Lord.
Warning that the Israelites must be kept away from their uncleanness so they do not die by making the Lord's dwelling place unclean.
Describes that anyone who is unclean and does not cleanse themselves shall be cut off from Israel because they have made the Lord's sanctuary unclean.
Repeats the principle that the unclean person who does not cleanse themselves shall be excluded from the assembly.
An early example of the expression 'cut off from their people' in connection with breaking holy regulations.
Concerns the covenant sign and the punishment of being cut off from the people for breaking the covenant.
